proposition: The Prologue, New Brethren and Sensorium call Bāysunghur Ibn Turka's second Timurid patron but none of the pages read dates the start of that patronage. The earliest dated Bāysunghur-linked items in the dissertation are Bazm u Razm and Suʾl al-Mulūk of 829/1426, then the Tuḥfa-yi ʿAlāʾiyya for Bāysunghur's son ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn (831/1428) and Nafsat al-Maṣdūr II (c. 832-35/1429-32); the dissertation's Munshaʾāt survey speaks of a close relationship, and lists one undated letter. The older project docs' 'second patron from c. 1416' is not found in any paper read.
